item.title: What Led to Maria Bartiromo’s Downfall at Fox News
item.description: The network this week took Maria Bartiromo off the air, pulling one of the last hosts whose coverage of Dominion Voting Systems drew an expensive defamation lawsuit.
item.dc:creator: Jim Rutenberg, Erik Wemple and Benjamin Mullin
item.media:description: Maria Bartiromo was among the Fox hosts whose coverage regarding conspiracy theories about Dominion voting machines was cited in a defamation lawsuit.

item.title: Will a Turnaround Plan Revive Volkswagen or Merely Delay Its Demise?
item.description: The beleaguered auto giant reached a deal with unions to cut tens of thousands of jobs and slash production. Is it enough to revive an iconic German company?
item.dc:creator: James Paton
item.media:description: A Volkswagen assembly line in Dresden, Germany. The automaker has won union approval for the most drastic restructuring in its 89-year history.

item.title: Authors Wrangle With Publishers Over $1.5 Billion Anthropic A.I. Settlement
item.description: The tech giant must pay $3,000 per pirated book that it used to train its chatbot. Many authors fear they could lose funds to others in the book business.
item.dc:creator: Neil Vigdor
item.media:credit: Jason Henry for The New York Times
item.media:description: An Anthropic logo at an event in San Francisco in May. The tech giant will have to pay more than $1.5 billion in a settlement over using books to train its chatbots.

item.title: Kenyans Made a Living Writing College Essays. Then A.I. Arrived.
item.description: Thousands of Kenyans made a living writing essays for overseas students. With A.I., the work has dried up, a warning for online gig work that has been a global lifeline.
item.dc:creator: Adam Satariano and Paul Mozur
item.media:credit: Kang-Chun Cheng for The New York Times
item.media:description: Teresios Bundi, who ran an essay-writing business catering to overseas students, said his experience with artificial intelligence was a warning for online gig workers.

item.title: California Forever’s Ambitious Plan Faces Another Setback
item.description: A legislative setback for a manufacturing and housing proposal shows how hard it remains to build in the largest state — and why a backlash against billionaires could make it even harder.
item.dc:creator: Conor Dougherty
item.media:credit: Aaron Wojack for The New York Times
item.media:description: California Forever has plans to build a new city, manufacturing and a shipyard in rural Solano County.

item.title: The Heart Drug Pelacarsen Fails, Shocking Novartis and Cardiologists
item.description: Doctors were hopeful the drug, which was being tested in a large clinical trial by Novartis, was going to be a powerful new tool to fight heart disease.
item.dc:creator: Gina Kolata
item.media:description: An illustration of lipoprotein(a), a low-density lipoprotein. Every study short of a randomized clinical trial had indicated that the drug would lower Lp(a) and help protect people from heart disease.

item.title: What to know about the report.
item.dc:creator: Sydney Ember

item.title: Trump Threatens to Halt Some Trade Unless the Fed Cuts Rates
item.description: The president said he could halt trade between the United States and countries with which it has a trade deficit if the central bank doesn’t do his bidding.
item.dc:creator: Tony Romm and Colby Smith
item.media:description: President Trump’s remarks were his latest attempt to pressure the Federal Reserve into lowering interest rates.

item.title: The U.S. Wants the Oil From These 17 Venezuelan Fields
item.description: A private oil company has struck a deal with the Trump administration to develop 17 areas in Venezuela, an effort that experts say will take years and billions of dollars.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca F. Elliott, Julie Turkewitz and Leanne Abraham
item.category: North American Blue Energy Partners Inc

item.title: How Gloria Steinem and Ms. Magazine Transformed the Publishing Industry
item.description: The feminist icon insisted that women were not a niche audience — and proved it in 1971 with the start of an influential publication owned and operated by them.
item.dc:creator: Katie Robertson
item.media:description: Gloria Steinem at the offices of Ms. magazine circa 1974 in New York City.

item.title: Tesla’s Cybercab Is Being Investigated by Federal Regulators
item.description: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said it would examine whether the company’s new self-driving taxi, which has no steering wheel, meets federal auto regulations.
item.dc:creator: Jack Ewing
item.media:description: A Tesla Cybercab in Austin, Texas, where the company has started offering paid rides in the driverless vehicles.

item.title: The Pros and Cons of Paying Off Your Mortgage Early
item.description: Homeowners who make extra payments can save thousands of dollars in interest. But, financial experts say, paying down other debt, with higher interest rates, may be a better option.
item.dc:creator: Ann Carrns

item.title: Robust Hiring Reinforces Strength of the U.S. Economy
item.description: Employers added 162,000 jobs and unemployment held at 4.1 percent last month, signs of a stability that contrasted with high inflation weighing on households and markets.
item.dc:creator: Sydney Ember

item.title: The job market in 2035: More nurses, fewer secretaries.

item.title: The Bond Markets Are Pushing Up Rates. Will Central Banks Follow?
item.description: Around the world, rising bond yields reflect shifting expectations on how fast policymakers will raise interest rates.

item.title: Notre Dame’s Jersey Patch Deal With SoFi Divides Alumni and Fans
item.description: Alumni have varying opinions about the school’s deal with the personal finance company SoFi to advertise on Notre Dame athletic uniforms.
item.dc:creator: Joe Drape and Tania Ganguli
item.media:description: The Notre Dame Fighting Irish taking the field before a game against Stanford at Notre Dame Stadium in October 2024.

item.title: Wineries Are Offering Bingo, Picnics, Jewelry … and Sometimes Wine
item.description: With slumping sales and fewer tourists, California winemakers have turned to special events and classes to woo customers — even those who don’t drink.

item.title: Iran War Helps to Drive U.S. Diesel Prices to New High
item.description: Because of the war in Iran, the cost has exceeded the record it hit in 2022 after Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
item.dc:creator: Gregory Schmidt
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:credit: Stella Kalinina for The New York Times

item.title: Former Labor Secretary Stoked Dysfunction and Toxicity, Department Report Finds
item.description: Lori Chavez-DeRemer spent Labor Department funds on personal travel and tolerated harassment in the agency, its inspector general found.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Davis O’Brien and Lydia DePillis
item.media:credit: Al Drago for The New York Times
item.media:description: A Labor Department report followed an investigation of a whistle-blower’s allegations against Lori Chavez-DeRemer, who resigned as labor secretary in April.

item.title: F.C.C. Asks Court to Toss ABC Suit Over Broadcast Licenses
item.description: The network sued the agency last month to stop it from taking steps that could force ABC stations off the air. The F.C.C. said the lawsuit was premature.
item.dc:creator: Jim Rutenberg
item.media:credit: Eric Lee for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Federal Communications Commission, which is led by Brendan Carr, said in a filing that ABC was trying to use a federal court to short-circuit the regulatory process.

item.title: Tesla Begins Offering Rides in a Car Without a Steering Wheel
item.description: The new Cybercab embodies Elon Musk’s vision of cars that drive themselves, but it is not clear when the vehicle will be widely available.
item.dc:creator: Jack Ewing
item.media:description: The Cybercab embodies the longtime ambition of Elon Musk, Tesla’s chief executive, to create cars that could steer, brake and navigate autonomously.

item.title: Volkswagen Plans to Cut 50,000 Jobs
item.description: Facing growing competition from China and rapidly advancing technology, the German auto giant said its board had approved a “comprehensive” overhaul.
item.dc:creator: James Paton
item.media:credit: Felix Schmitt for The New York Times
item.media:description: Facing intense pressure and Chinese competition, Volkswagen has slashed its annual production targets and plans to cut its model lineup.

item.title: Mortgage Rates Hit 6.71%, Their Highest Level Since July 2025
item.description: Higher costs for home loans have put a squeeze on the housing market, adding pressure to consumers already struggling with elevated inflation.

item.title: Maria Bartiromo Is Out at Fox News
item.description: The dismissal came after Ms. Bartiromo shared internal Fox Business communications with the White House, a person familiar with the details confirmed.
item.dc:creator: Erik Wemple
item.media:description: Fox did not give a reason for Maria Bartiromo’s abrupt departure. She has been an ardent supporter of President Trump.

item.title: Bessent Blames Ukraine for High Energy Prices
item.description: After meeting with Russia’s finance minister, the Treasury secretary said Ukraine’s attacks on Russian oil infrastructure were contributing to a global energy shock driven mainly by the U.S. war with Iran.

item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
Regime Change: Inside the Imperial Presidency of Donald Trump (Book)
item.media:description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is facing a complicated challenge as he tries to cool global energy prices while increasing economic pressure on Iran.

item.title: Leon Black Sues Congressional Panel Investigating Epstein
item.description: The billionaire skipped a deposition on Thursday and filed a lawsuit seeking to block a House committee’s subpoenas demanding nondisclosure agreements he may have made with women.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Goldstein and Michael Gold

item.media:description: Leon Black, left, leaving the Rayburn House Office Building in June after he cut short his interview with the House Oversight Committee about Jeffrey Epstein.

item.title: The Athletic Says Dianna Russini’s Relationship With Mike Vrabel Violated Its Standards
item.description: The New York Times-owned publication said the relationship between its former reporter Dianna Russini and Mike Vrabel of the Patriots gave the appearance of a conflict of interest.
item.dc:creator: Ken Belson and Katherine Rosman
item.media:description: Dianna Russini at an N.F.L. game in September 2019. As an N.F.L. insider, she was focused on getting scoops about players and coaches.

item.title: Schools Giving Aid to Minority Students Could Lose Tax Exemptions Under Trump’s New Rules
item.description: The Treasury Department released rules that would prevent schools with race-based programs from qualifying for tax-exempt status, a threat to both higher education and other private schools.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Duehren and Michael C. Bender
item.media:credit: Sophie Park for The New York Times
item.media:description: Schools like Harvard could be at risk of losing their tax-exempt status under the new rules.

item.title: U.S. Trade Gap Ballooned in July

item.title: Rate Rise in Play as Fed Officials Await Inflation Data
item.description: Christopher J. Waller, a Federal Reserve governor, sounded optimistic about inflation’s trajectory but indicated he would support higher rates if progress does not continue.
item.dc:creator: Colby Smith
item.media:description: Christopher Waller, a Federal Reserve governor, said he was looking for evidence that showed inflation was continuing to abate.

item.title: Nvidia Buys Hugging Face in $12.9 Billion Deal
item.description: The acquisition of the start-up is an indication of Nvidia’s growing role as Silicon Valley’s central banker and its emphasis on open-source technology.
item.dc:creator: Kalley Huang, Lauren Hirsch and Kate Conger
item.media:credit: Manuel Orbegozo for The New York Times
item.media:description: Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s chief executive, has overseen the company as its quarterly profits have increased tenfold. The company is spending those resources on acquisitions, including of Hugging Face.

item.title: Oil Jumps for Fourth Straight Day and Diesel Nears Record High
item.description: This week’s renewed strikes by the United States and Iran strain the flow of energy and diminish expectations the disruption will end soon.

item.title: Which Investors Will Get Rich From Anthropic’s IPO?
item.description: When Anthropic goes public in a blockbuster offering, which investors will profit? The answer says a lot about how much start-up investing has changed over the years.

item.title: Why the Courts Are Hesitant to Punish Tech Giants Like Meta and Google
item.description: After finding antitrust violations, federal courts have been reluctant to impose harsh sanctions. They fear meddling in markets where technology is racing ahead.

item.media:description: Creating effective remedies is difficult for the courts, particularly because of the rapid pace of change in the tech industry.

item.title: Southwest to Open Premium Airport Lounges Across the Country

item.media:description: Austin-Bergstrom International Airport, in Texas, is one of four airports that could be getting a Southwest Airlines premium lounge starting late next year.

item.title: Employer Health Costs Are Expected to Spike in 2027
item.description: A new U.S. survey anticipates an average increase of 11 percent unless benefits are cut, the highest rate in decades. Other findings also predict a sharp rise.
item.dc:creator: Reed Abelson
item.media:credit: Morgan Lieberman for The New York Times
item.media:description: U.S. employers are bracing for what looks to be the sharpest increase in health care costs in more than two decades.

item.title: Saturday Evening Post Will Stop Printing After 205 Years

item.media:description: The Saturday Evening Post cover from May 29, 1943.

item.title: Get to Know Your Phone’s Built-In Emergency Kit
item.description: In times of natural disasters and other dangers, special features tucked away on your iPhone or Android device could help make a difference.
item.dc:creator: J. D. Biersdorfer
item.media:description: Apple’s more recent iPhone models include the ability to communicate with emergency services by text chat over a satellite connection, as well as a demonstration mode.

item.title: Inside the Fight Against a Flesh-Eating Fly in Mexico
item.description: For the first time in a year, the U.S.-Mexico border partly reopened to cattle imports following a screwworm infestation across the region. The battle against the flesh-eating fly has only just begun deep in Mexico.
item.dc:creator: James Wagner and Luis Antonio Rojas
item.media:credit: Luis Antonio Rojas for The New York Times
item.media:description: New World screwworm flies in a cage at a facility in Metapa, Mexico, that that produces sterile flies, which when released into the wild slowly reduce the population size.

item.title: Missouri Voters Appear to Recall City Councilman Over Data Center Support
item.description: Initial results showed that residents of Independence, Mo., voted overwhelmingly to recall an official who backed billions of dollars in tax breaks for a data center.
item.dc:creator: David McCabe and Lauren McCarthy
item.media:credit: Clayton Steward for The New York Times
item.media:description: Organizers of the recall vote said the councilman, John Perkins, had failed to engage the public while the city negotiated with the developer of a data center project.

item.title: Bill Simmons’s Co-Hosts Are Tired of His A.I. Antics
item.description: The founder of The Ringer is taking flak for using artificial intelligence to conjure opinions from the deceased film critic Roger Ebert. Ads from OpenAI have recently run on the show.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Mullin
item.media:credit: Mike Windle/Getty Images for Vanity Fair
item.media:description: Film buffs are complaining that the podcast host Bill Simmons used artificial intelligence to approximate the opinions of the critic Roger Ebert, who died in 2013.
